title: The Tonic Triad band and its members and instruments
summary: Clark names the Tonic Triad, how the Depression ended it, and lists members and what they played.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: I have the picture of some of it up there. The late Tonic Triad, not the original Tonic Triad. I have a picture of the late Tonic Triad. Well after the Depression, you know, those fellas, they didn't have no money, you know, no job or nothing. The man just lost all interest in music. So I was lucky because I had a job. I was very lucky. I had a job all during Depression. Very lucky. And I thank God Almighty for it. So he couldn't get those fellas together anymore, you know. So, all right, so now I'm going to go, I'll go to the record now. You want to stop the record? Cut that off, cut that off.
Well, yes. Al C. Landry, Willie Paggio, Willie Wilson, Johnny Wilson.
Now what instruments did they play?

Johnny Wilson played baritone. Willie Wilson and Willie Paggio played trumpet. And Landry, did you name it? Al C. He trumpet. Al C. would die. Yeah, that's right. And Andrew Stevens played bass. Oscar Grammer played bass, which Oscar, they tell me he has a stroke now. I don't know, I haven't saw him in years, I don't know. And as I told you, Johnny Wilson was baritone. And a fellow by the name of William Eber, he was a Jamaican, he played baritone. And a fellow by the name of Jones, he played clarinet. And Oscar Henry, trombone, I played trombone there. A fellow by the name of Tom Steptoe, which is past, he played trombone. And let's see who else now. There's a lot of them in there that I didn't know very well, but those men that I called I knew very well. Now the drummers was Albert Francis, he was a snare drummer. And this fellow Peter Raphael, which is Lost One Limb, he was the bass drummer. Fine drummers, both of them, read like anything. And let me see, oh yeah, a fellow by the name of Gil, he played alto, which we called the ! And a lot of others that I didn't know very well. I just knew them by sight, you know.
